items.s: In 2025, France ____ less wine than in any year since 1957.

tfn.s: France expects to make less wine this year than last year.
tfn.why: The text says the harvest “would be 2% less than last year”.

tfn.s: Every French wine region produced less this year.
tfn.why: Bordeaux is the opposite: production there “is expected to rise by 10%”.

tfn.s: Champagne growers picked their grapes earlier than usual.
tfn.why: The heat made the grapes build up sugar quickly, so growers “had to pick much earlier than normal”.

tfn.s: French wine will be more expensive this year.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text talks about amounts and quality but says nothing about prices.

tfn.s: Bordeaux expects to produce 12% more wine than last year.
tfn.why: Bordeaux is up 10%. The 12% rise is for the south-west.

pre.d: the time when farmers pick the plants or fruit they have grown

focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word such as up or down. The small word changes the meaning, so learn the two words together.

items.s: In hot weather, sugar can build ____ in the grapes very quickly.

Growers sometimes cut ____ the number of grapes on each vine.
Even in a heatwave, many growers carry ____ working in the early morning.
Higher prices can partly ____ the loss of income when a harvest is small.
Warmer winters have ____ the ripening of the fruit, so growers now pick weeks earlier than their grandparents did.
When time is short, a grower may have to ____ flavour to protect the rest of the crop.
Rather than hoping for cooler weather, many farms are investing in ____ to hotter conditions.
A delayed delivery is a minor ____, but a failed crop can threaten a whole business.
Hot weather lowers the ____ of grapes, which can make the wine taste flat.

tfn.s: Both 2025 and 2026 were weak years for French wine production.
tfn.why: 2025 was the weakest since 1957, and 2026 is expected to be 2% below it and 14% below the five-year average.

tfn.s: Bordeaux's production fell this year because its planted area was cut.
tfn.why: Production there is expected to rise 10% despite a 5% reduction in planted area.

tfn.s: Southern growers began leaving more foliage on their vines because of a government programme.
tfn.why: The text says earlier heat pushed growers to change, but it does not mention any programme.

tfn.s: Bordeaux's production this year is still below its recent average.
tfn.why: It is up 10% on last year but “still leaves it 11% below the recent average”.

tfn.s: The south-west's production is far above its level of the previous four years.
tfn.why: The text calls its rise “essentially a return to its previous four-year level”.

focus.note: Many phrasal verbs have more than one meaning, so read the whole sentence before you choose. Some also take an object and a preposition, as in 'put off' something.

tfn.s: Bordeaux's production rose even though it had less land under vines.
tfn.why: The text gives a 10% increase on 2025 “despite a 5% cut in planted area”.

tfn.s: The writer treats the south's result as proof that heat explains the whole pattern.
tfn.why: The writer says heat alone does not explain it, since the hottest regions did not suffer most.

tfn.s: The writer expects the ministry's estimates to prove too low.
tfn.why: The text stresses that these are estimates and that the final accounting comes later, but it never predicts which way they will move.

tfn.s: The writer implies that Mandois's comments are a poor guide to the whole vintage.

focus.note: At this level many phrasal verbs are fixed with a certain kind of object or a following preposition: bear out a claim, stem from a cause, tide someone over. Learn them in these frames.

items.s: The ministry's caution is borne ____ by how far final results often differ from the early forecasts.

speak.title: Role-play: a price rise for house wine
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your wine supplier says the price of your house wine will go up by 10%. You don't want to pass the cost on to customers. Ask why the price is rising and ask for a better deal.

b.text: Hot summers have made wine harvests smaller, so your costs are higher. Explain why the price must rise. You can offer a small discount if the restaurant orders more.

phrases: Why is the price going up?
I'm afraid the harvest was smaller than usual.
We can't pass that cost on to our customers.
Could you give us a discount if we order more?
I'd be happy to meet you halfway.
That's the best price I can offer.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree a price, and was it fair for both sides?
